issues.description: Field Farm.animals: The problem statement and UML (problem_statement.md lines 16-21 and 108-111) specify that Farm has an attribute 'animals: List<Animal>' and explicitly instruct to initialize it with an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The template Farm.java currently contains a TODO to implement Farm but does not declare the field (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-6). The solution implements the field as 'private Queue<Animal> animals' and initializes it with 'new LinkedList<>()', exposing getter/setter and methods using Queue (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13). This mismatch between the specified List/ArrayList and the solution's Queue/LinkedList is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which collection type to implement, how to write the constructor and accessors, and which semantics (List vs Queue) the tests or grading expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across the artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: change the solution (and tests, if any) to declare 'private List<Animal> animals;', initialize it in the no-arg constructor with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', and update getter/setter and uses to accept/return List<Animal>. Alternatively, if FIFO behavior was intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify 'animals: Queue<Animal>' and instruct to initialize with 'new LinkedList<>()', and update the textual instructions that currently mention ArrayList.

issues.description: Concept: the Farm's collection of animals. In the problem statement (problem_statement.md) the Farm's animal container is described as a List implemented using an ArrayList and students are instructed to "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments" and to provide getter/setter and addAnimal semantics that match a List. In the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) the corresponding field is declared as private Queue<Animal> animals and initialized with new LinkedList<>(), and addAnimal uses Queue.offer(...) semantics. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) contains a TODO to implement Farm but no animals field yet. This naming/type mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) and different API (add() vs offer()) means a student reading the problem statement and then inspecting the reference solution or expected API may be confused about which collection type to use and which methods to call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type and API consistent across artifacts. Option A (align to problem statement): change the solution to declare the field as private List<Animal> animals; initialize it with new ArrayList<>(); change addAnimal to animals.add(a); and update getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Option B (align to solution): relax the problem statement text to describe the animal container as a generic queue/collection (e.g. "a collection of animals, e.g. a Queue or List") and remove the explicit requirement to use ArrayList so the documentation matches the reference implementation. Prefer Option A if the exercise intends to teach use of ArrayList/List APIs; prefer Option B if queue semantics were intentionally used in tests.
